title: Optional local-inference install resolves vulnerable adm-zip parser

affectedLocations.label: root_control
affectedLocations.detail: Lockfile resolves adm-zip@0.5.17, affected by the advisory.

affectedLocations.label: wrapper
affectedLocations.detail: onnxruntime-node@1.24.3 install-time wrapper depends on adm-zip ^0.5.16.

affectedLocations.label: entrypoint
affectedLocations.detail: Supported optional local-transformers provider imports the dependency chain.

affectedLocations.label: entrypoint

attackerControlledSource: A crafted NuGet ZIP supplied from a compromised/malicious package feed, configured HTTPS proxy, or equivalent installation supply-chain position.
sinkOrBrokenControl: onnxruntime-node@1.24.3 postinstall loads the downloaded .nupkg with adm-zip@0.5.17; vulnerable adm-zip eagerly allocates the attacker-declared uncompressed size before validating actual data/CRC.
impact: Multi-gigabyte allocation can terminate the npm/OpenClaw installation process or exhaust host memory when the optional local inference dependency is installed.
plausibility: The checked-in lockfile selects the affected version. Upstream package evidence retained under artifacts/01_context/advisory_evidence proves a default Linux x64 postinstall path invokes AdmZip on a network-fetched NuGet package.
closestControl: TLS, registry integrity metadata, and a fixed Microsoft/NuGet feed constrain the source, but do not protect after feed/proxy compromise; the vulnerable parser itself lacks the fixed allocation bound.

candidateLocalValidation.method: lockfile inspection, current npm audit, and exact upstream tarball source trace
candidateLocalValidation.evidence: package-lock.json:64-75, 893-901, 1624-1640 plus retained onnxruntime-node install scripts
candidateLocalValidation.proofGap: No safe OOM PoC executed because doing so would be destructive; advisory regression/fix evidence demonstrates the allocation primitive.

candidateLocalAttackPath.sink: adm-zip@0.5.17 eager Buffer allocation from declared uncompressed size
preconditions: Linux x64 default CUDA package acquisition or forced install
attacker can influence the fetched package bytes through supply-chain/proxy compromise
